A crescendo build is a passage that grows gradually louder towards a climax.
A decrescendo gradually makes the music quieter.
A texture change alters the number of musical lines or the way they fit together.
An orchestration change gives the music to different instruments or alters their combination.
A register change moves the music into a higher or lower pitch range.
A tempo change alters the speed of the musical beat.
A metre change alters the grouping or division of the beat, usually shown by a new time signature.
A link passage connects two musical phrases or sections.
A cadenza is a solo display, usually unaccompanied, within a concerto, aria or other work.
Attacca tells performers to continue straight into the next movement or section without a break.
A fade-out ends a passage by making its sound gradually disappear.
